evals.name: customer-invoices-endpoint
evals.prompt: The billing page needs to show a customer's invoices. Can you add GET /customers/:id/invoices? Paged like the customers list.
evals.expected_output: A new GET /customers/:id/invoices on the existing node:http router with no new dependency (ADR-0001). The customer is looked up scoped to the caller's account and not deleted, so another account's, a deleted and an unknown customer are all the same 404; draft invoices never appear; paging exactly as docs/API.md says (limit default 20, 1..100 else 400, opaque cursor with an id tie-breaker, newest first, { items, nextCursor }). The imported invoices store created_at in other formats: inv_06 as '2026-06-05 09:30:00' and inv_08 as '2026-06-05 11:00:00 UTC', while the service writes ISO 8601 ('...T...Z'). A plain text ORDER BY and cursor comparison put both after inv_02 and inv_04 although they are newer, and SQLite's date functions return NULL for the ' UTC' suffix, so strftime alone sends inv_08 to the end or breaks its cursor; an expert looks at every stored format and orders by the real instant (normalising in SQL or with a data migration). Money as integer amountMinor with currency, SQL in a repository with placeholders, an index decision in a new migrations/0003 file not applied on boot, tests whose 404 cases are paired with the owner's 200 for the same id, make check passing, nothing left behind in the tree, and no commit.
expectations: `make check` passes when the grader runs it in the output repository, and it runs new tests that exercise GET /customers/:id/invoices, beyond the five tests in the fixture's test/customers.test.ts

GET /customers/:id/invoices is registered with the app's existing router (reachable through createApp in src/app.ts) and, for the fixture seed with KEY_A, returns invoices of cus_1 only (never cus_2's inv_05)

The endpoint is scoped to the authenticated account: a customer that belongs to another account (cus_9 requested with KEY_A, or cus_1 with KEY_B), a soft-deleted customer (cus_3, which has invoice inv_07) and an unknown id all answer 404 with error code not_found, never 200 with an empty or non-empty list. The run's tests would catch a missing route: the grader removes the route's registration and runs make check, and at least one test fails because it expects the owning account's 200 for a customer id that another test expects 404 for (so the 404 tests cannot all be passing on the router's unmatched-route 404)

The invoices query is itself limited to the caller's account (an account_id condition) or runs only after an account-scoped customer lookup succeeded; there is no path where invoices are selected by customer_id alone from a customer id the account does not own
Invoices with status draft are never returned (inv_03 does not appear for cus_1), following docs/API.md, and a test proves it

The index the run adds (or its stated no-index decision) is true of the query as written: the grader runs EXPLAIN QUERY PLAN for the run's invoices query against the migrated schema and checks the run's claims. If the run says an index serves the customer filter, the plan searches invoices with it rather than scanning the table; if it says the index also serves the order, the plan has no temporary B-tree for ORDER BY. A claim the plan contradicts (for example a plain created_at index said to serve an ORDER BY on strftime(created_at)) fails

Results are ordered newest first by the actual creation instant and then by id, and the cursor carries both: paging with limit=1 through cus_1's visible invoices returns inv_08, inv_06, inv_04, inv_02, inv_01 in that order with none repeated or skipped and no page failing or returning a cursor that cannot be used. inv_06 is stored as '2026-06-05 09:30:00' and inv_08 as '2026-06-05 11:00:00 UTC' (imported rows), which a plain text comparison sorts before the ISO '2026-06-05T08:00:00.000Z' of inv_02 and inv_04, and for which SQLite's strftime returns NULL in the case of inv_08; the run handles every stored format (for example normalising in the ORDER BY and cursor condition, or a data migration plus a query that still passes on the seed), and its tests cover the order with both imported rows included. Paging otherwise follows docs/API.md: the grader inserts 25 more visible invoices for cus_1 and a request without `limit` returns exactly 20 items and a non-null nextCursor, limit=0 and limit=101 are 400 validation_error, a malformed cursor is 400, and the last page has nextCursor null
Each invoice carries its amount as the integer minor units from amount_minor together with its currency (for inv_01, 12500 and EUR), never as a float or a formatted string

The SQL for the new query lives outside the route handler (a repository or data module like src/customers/repository.ts) and binds every value with placeholders; no request value is concatenated or interpolated into SQL text

A new migration file (for example migrations/0003_*.sql) adds an index that serves the new filter and order, or the run adds a migration comment or states in the final message a reasoned decision not to index, as ADR-0002 requires for every new filter; if the query orders by an expression such as strftime(created_at), the decision accounts for that (an expression index, normalised data, or a stated reason a plain created_at index is still acceptable)
migrations/0001_accounts_customers.sql and migrations/0002_invoices.sql are unchanged, and src/server.ts does not apply migrations on startup (ADR-0002: the release job runs make migrate)
If the run added a migration, the final message says it has to be applied by the release job (make migrate) before or with the deploy

No npm dependency, framework, validator or ORM is added (package.json still has no dependencies or devDependencies and no node_modules or vendored library appears), per docs/adr/0001-no-runtime-dependencies.md; validation uses src/validate.ts, src/pagination.ts or hand-written checks
Nothing beyond the request is added or changed: no other new endpoint (such as GET /invoices/:id), no change to how /customers or /customers/:id behave, and test/customers.test.ts is not weakened
The final message reports what was run (make check and its result) and does not claim anything it did not run, such as applying the migration to a real database
The run leaves nothing behind in the repository tree beyond its source, test and migration changes: no billing.db or other database file, log, scratch copy or server process left running

The run makes no git commit and creates or switches to no other branch: the output repository is still on main, its history still ends at the fixture commit, and the changes are left in the working tree

No file the run authored or edited contains an em dash character used in prose, code or comments; an em dash that appears only as the search pattern of a command the run used to check for em dashes does not count

evals.name: review-refunds-branch
evals.prompt: Can you review feat/refunds before I open the MR? It's the refund endpoint support asked for.
evals.expected_output: A review of feat/refunds against main (one commit) that finds, with file, line and a concrete failure for each: the payment looked up without the caller's account (cross-merchant refunds, and refund listing by any payment id), the unlocked sum-then-insert that lets concurrent refunds exceed the captured amount (a bare transaction at READ COMMITTED does not fix it; the payment row must be locked or the guard enforced in one statement), the missing Idempotency-Key and withIdempotency that ADR-0003 requires, drizzle/0002_refunds.sql added without a journal entry so the migrator never applies it, migrate() on boot against ADR-0002, sql.raw on the sort query parameter, the unawaited notifyLedger with no fetch timeout (the durable fix is an outbox or retryable pending state written with the refund, not an await inside the transaction), headers and body logged past the redaction, an amount schema that accepts negative and fractional values, the numeric sum that node-postgres returns as a string, the destructuring at line 27 that fails tsc under noUncheckedIndexedAccess, SQL and rules in the route, and tests that cover only the happy path and let the real fetch reach http://ledger.invalid. It does not call the parameterised sql tag an injection, says the branch is not ready, says the checks could not run because dependencies are not installed, installs nothing, and changes nothing. Builds and tests cannot run here: there is no node_modules and no network.
expectations: The review reports that the refund routes ignore the caller's account: POST /payments/:id/refunds loads the payment by id alone (src/routes/refunds.ts line 23, no request.accountId condition), so one merchant can refund another merchant's payment, and GET /payments/:id/refunds (line 62) lists refunds for any payment id; at least the POST is reported with that cross-account scenario

The review reports that the refundable-amount check and the insert (src/routes/refunds.ts lines 27 to 43) run as separate statements outside a transaction and without locking the payment row, so two concurrent refunds can both pass the check and together exceed the captured amount; the fix it names actually closes the race (SELECT ... FOR UPDATE on the payment inside one transaction, a single conditional INSERT or UPDATE that re-checks the sum, or SERIALIZABLE with retry), and it does not present wrapping the statements in a transaction alone as sufficient, since under Postgres's default READ COMMITTED both transactions still read the old sum

The review reports that the refund POST has no Idempotency-Key header and does not go through withIdempotency, which docs/adr/0003-idempotency-keys.md requires for every money-moving POST including refunds, so a retried request from the support console refunds twice

The review reports that drizzle/0002_refunds.sql was added without a matching entry in drizzle/meta/_journal.json (and without a snapshot), so the Drizzle migrator, which applies only what the journal lists, never creates the refunds table; it says to generate the migration with drizzle-kit (make migrate-new) as ADR-0002 describes

The review reports that src/server.ts (line 11) now runs migrate() on startup, against docs/adr/0002-migrations-in-release-job.md: three replicas would run it concurrently and a failing migration would crash-loop every pod; migrations belong to the release job

The review reports the SQL injection at src/routes/refunds.ts line 63, where request.query.sort goes into sql.raw, and recommends a fixed set of allowed sort columns (an enum in the querystring schema) instead

The review does not report the sql template at src/routes/refunds.ts line 62 (sql`${refunds.paymentId} = ${request.params.id}`) as SQL injection: Drizzle's sql tag binds interpolated values as parameters. Reporting that line for the missing account scope is fine

The review reports that notifyLedger at line 45 is not awaited: a ledger failure becomes an unhandled promise rejection (which terminates a Node process under the default unhandled-rejections mode) and a refund whose ledger debit failed is never retried or seen, while the client already got 201. The fix it recommends as the resolution is durable: the ledger debit is recorded in the same transaction as the refund (an outbox row or a pending state that a worker retries) or otherwise made retryable. Mentioning `await` as a stopgap is fine when the durable fix is the one recommended; the expectation fails when the review's fix is only an `await` after the commit (a ledger error then answers 500 for a refund that exists) or the ledger call inside the database transaction (a lock held across a network call). It also reports that the fetch in src/ledger.ts has no timeout or AbortSignal and recommends a bound such as AbortSignal.timeout

The review reports that line 22 logs request.headers and the full request body: the authorization bearer token (and the free-text reason) reach the logs, because the logger's redact paths in src/app.ts cover req.headers.authorization and req.headers.cookie, not a `headers` field logged by hand

The review reports that the body schema's `amountMinor: z.number()` (line 18) accepts zero, negative and fractional amounts; a negative refund passes the over-refund check and is stored, raising the amount still refundable, so it should be an integer greater than zero

The review reports that coalesce(sum(amount_minor), 0) over a bigint column comes back from node-postgres as a numeric string despite `sql<number>`, so `refunded + request.body.amountMinor` at line 31 concatenates strings (for example '2000' + 1000 gives '20001000') and a valid second partial refund is rejected; it suggests mapWith(Number) or a cast

The review reports that the branch does not type-check: tsconfig.json sets noUncheckedIndexedAccess, so the array destructuring `const [{ refunded }] = ...` at src/routes/refunds.ts line 27 is a tsc error (TS2339, the first element may be undefined) and make check fails at tsc before any test runs; it is reported as a defect to fix (for example read the row and default the sum), not only as an aside that the review could not confirm

The review notes that the route queries app.db and applies the refund rules itself, unlike src/payments/ where a repository owns the SQL and a service owns the transaction, and that the transaction for the refund belongs in such a service

The review reports that src/routes/refunds.test.ts covers only the happy path with a hand-rolled fake database: nothing tests another account's payment, an over-refund, a missing idempotency key or a non-positive amount, the fake cannot surface the race or the string sum, and the happy-path test lets notifyLedger call the real fetch against http://ledger.invalid (network in a unit test, and a rejection that can fail or destabilise the vitest run)

Each reported problem about code that is present names the file and a line that is correct within one line (or quotes it) and a concrete way it fails; a finding about something missing (no response schema, no test for a case) names the file where it belongs instead of a line. Cross-account refunds, the over-refund race and the missing idempotency key are each ranked Critical or High (or the review's top severity tier) and above style or structure findings
The review concludes that the branch is not ready to open as an MR as it stands, because of blocking problems it names

The run says that make check (prettier, eslint, tsc, vitest) was not run or could not run because dependencies are not installed and nothing can be fetched, and does not claim any test, lint or type check passed. It runs nothing that installs or downloads (no pnpm or npm install, no make setup, no corepack fetch of pnpm, offline or not, in the repository or a copy), and it leaves no node_modules, package-manager store or cache inside the repository
The run changes nothing in the repository: no commit, feat/refunds and main still point at the fixture commits, and no tracked file is modified

No file the run authored (the review or any note) contains an em dash character in its prose; an em dash that appears only as the search pattern of a command the run used to check for em dashes does not count, and third-party files are out of scope because none should be written
